def build_run_report(session: Session, run: Run) -> RunReport:
    """Build the redacted, GX-agnostic report for a terminal ``run``."""
    suite = session.get(Suite, run.suite_id)
    connection = session.get(Connection, suite.connection_id) if suite is not None else None
    asset = run_service.resolve_asset(session, suite, run)
    owner = _resolve_owner(session, asset, suite)
    checks = {c.id: c for c in session.scalars(select(Check).where(Check.suite_id == run.suite_id))}
    # The warehouse's own column classifications (G3, #433) — the same governance floor the REST and
    # MCP read paths apply.
    tags = effective_column_tags(session, asset)
    results: list[Result] = run_service.list_results(session, run.id)
    # The check as of THIS result (#1489/#1880/#1613) — the card's label, the redactors'
    # column + type and `zero_sample_suppressed`'s kind/engine all read the same snapshot
    # REST/MCP use, so a check re-pointed between the run and a late delivery never
    # relabels the result or redacts it against the wrong column. One `check_versions` read.
    as_of = run_service.historical_check_snapshots(session, results, checks)
    # Resolved once per report (#1887), not per result.
    zero_sample_mode = privacy_settings_service.zero_sample_mode(session)

    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    check_reports: list[CheckReport] = []
    for result in results:
        counts[result.status] = counts.get(result.status, 0) + 1
        check = checks.get(result.check_id)
        snap = as_of[result.id]
        # Column-aware redaction (#415): the tested column (as of the result, #1613) surfaces when
        # non-PII; the suite policy + heuristics mask PII. The tracker names what was masked and
        # why (#2255), the same pair REST and MCP return.
        redacted = run_service.redact_sample_failures_with_state(
            result.sample_failures,
            tested_column=snap.column,
            policy=suite.column_policy if suite is not None else None,
            tags=tags,
        )
        check_reports.append(
            CheckReport(
                check_id=result.check_id,
                check_name=check.name if check is not None else "(deleted check)",
                expectation_type=snap.expectation_type or "",
                status=result.status,
                metric_value=(
                    float(result.metric_value) if result.metric_value is not None else None
                ),
                observed_value=run_service.redact_observed_value(
                    result.observed_value,
                    tested_column=snap.column,
                    expectation_type=snap.expectation_type,
                    policy=suite.column_policy if suite is not None else None,
                    tags=tags,
                ),
                expected_value=result.expected_value,
                sample_summary=redacted.sample,
                redacted_columns=tuple(redacted.redacted_columns),
                redaction_reasons=redacted.redaction_reasons,
                sample_suppressed=run_service.zero_sample_suppressed(
                    status=result.status,
                    check_kind=snap.kind,
                    engine=snap.engine,
                    zero_sample_mode=zero_sample_mode,
                ),
            )
        )

    worst = worst_severity(r.status for r in results)
    incidents = _incident_cards(session, run, results, checks)
    return RunReport(
        run_id=run.id,
        suite_id=run.suite_id,
        suite_name=suite.name if suite is not None else "(deleted suite)",
        run_status=run.status,
        datasource_type=connection.type if connection is not None else "",
        target_label=_target_label(suite),
        worst_severity=worst,
        counts=counts,
        checks=check_reports,

Both `column_tags` (the warehouse source + the effective map) and `column_detections` (the
profiler source, ADR 0049) speak it, and `column_tags` reads `column_detections` lazily when it
builds the map; keeping the shared words here is what keeps that edge one-directional.

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Final

#: Normalized outputs of every classification source.
SENSITIVE: Final[str] = "sensitive"
NON_SENSITIVE: Final[str] = "public"
#: A profiler detection (ADR 0049), overlaid by `effective_column_tags` on columns with no
#: warehouse verdict. Deliberately a THIRD value: it is in neither the sensitive-tag set (so it
#: is not the floor — the suite's `identifier_column` clears it) nor the clearing set (so it
#: never satisfies fail-closed clearance).
DETECTED: Final[str] = "detected"


def fold_key(column: str) -> str:
    """The redaction map's key for a column name: stripped and lower-cased, the one folding every
    rung (warehouse tags, inheritance, detections, the policy lookups) agrees on."""
    return column.strip().lower()


class EffectiveColumnTags(dict[str, str]):
    """The column→verdict map plus WHICH `sensitive` entries arrived through lineage rather than
    from the column's own warehouse tag (#2255). A plain dict to every existing reader — equality,
    `.get`, JSON — so the provenance can never change a verdict; the redaction reasons read it."""

    def __init__(self, tags: dict[str, str], *, inherited: frozenset[str] = frozenset()) -> None:
        super().__init__(tags)
        self.inherited = inherited


def inherited_tag_columns(tags: object) -> frozenset[str]:

# `redacted_columns` on every surface that shows the list. Ordered as the ladder consults them.
RedactionReason = Literal[
    "own_tag",  # the column's own warehouse classification (G3 floor)
    "inherited_tag",  # `sensitive` inherited through recorded column lineage (#1710)
    "policy",  # the suite's `pii_columns`
    "unclassified",  # fail-closed mode (`require_classification`) and nothing cleared it
    "detected",  # the profiler found PII-shaped values at profile time (ADR 0049)
    "classifier",  # the read-time name / value heuristic affirmatively says PII
    "default_mask",  # an incidental column nobody classified — precautionary (#415)
]
REDACTION_REASONS: tuple[RedactionReason, ...] = (
    "own_tag",

    "classifier",

)

    column: str,

# Redaction summary surfaced beside `sample_failures` (#424/#415); `zero_sample` (#1873)
# distinguishes a null sample SUPPRESSED by zero-sample mode (#1676) from one that was
# genuinely empty — both read `null` on the wire otherwise.
RedactionState = Literal["full", "partial", "none", "zero_sample"]


@dataclass
class _RedactionTracker:
    """Accumulates per-column show/mask decisions across one `redact_sample_failures`
    call, so the caller can report an honest summary instead of re-sniffing the
    redacted output for the `"<redacted>"` sentinel (fragile — a genuine cell value
    equal to the sentinel would misreport, and it can't see counts).
    """

    column_state: dict[str, bool] = field(default_factory=dict)
    column_reason: dict[str, RedactionReason] = field(default_factory=dict)
    anonymous_masked: bool = False

    def record(
        self, column: str | None, shown: bool, reason: RedactionReason | None = None
    ) -> None:
        if column:
            self.column_state[column] = self.column_state.get(column, False) or shown
            if not shown and reason is not None:
                # The ladder is deterministic per column within one sample, so the first masked
                # reason is THE reason; keeping it (not the last) makes that an invariant.
                self.column_reason.setdefault(column, reason)
        elif not shown:
            self.anonymous_masked = True

    def summary(self) -> tuple[RedactionState | None, list[str]]:
        """`(state, redacted_columns)`. ``state`` is ``None`` when nothing data-bearing was seen
        (e.g. only aggregate counts, or an empty sample) — there is nothing true to claim either
        way, so the caller should omit any redaction label rather than guess.
        ``redacted_columns`` lists columns that were masked everywhere they appeared (never
        shown).
        """
        shown_any = any(self.column_state.values())
        masked_any = any(not shown for shown in self.column_state.values()) or self.anonymous_masked
        redacted_columns = sorted(name for name, shown in self.column_state.items() if not shown)
        if not shown_any and not masked_any:
            return None, []
        if masked_any and not shown_any:
            return "full", redacted_columns
        if shown_any and not masked_any:
            return "none", redacted_columns
        return "partial", redacted_columns

    def reasons(self) -> dict[str, RedactionReason]:
        """Why each entry of ``redacted_columns`` was masked (#2255) — the same key set, every
        time: a masked column whose rung went unrecorded is a bug, not a blank, so it is reported
        as ``default_mask`` (the precautionary reading) rather than dropped."""
        return {
            name: self.column_reason.get(name, "default_mask")
            for name, shown in sorted(self.column_state.items())
            if not shown
        }

    session: Session,
    *,
    version: int,
    name: str,
    description: str | None,
    checks: list[dict[str, Any]],
    connection_id: uuid.UUID,
    created_by: uuid.UUID,
) -> Suite:
    """Create a new suite + checks from a document, bound to `connection_id`."""
    connection = _load_target_connection(session, version, connection_id)
    # Validate every check up front so a bad document writes nothing.
    source_ids = [_validate_check(session, connection, c) for c in checks]

    suite = Suite(
        name=name,
        description=description,
        connection_id=connection_id,
        created_by=created_by,
    )
    suite.checks = [
        Check(
            name=c["name"],
            kind=c["kind"],
            engine=c.get("engine", GX_ENGINE),
            expectation_type=c["expectation_type"],
            # Key ABSENT (an older document) → derive, so an import behaves like fresh authoring.
            dimension=(
                validate_dimension(c["dimension"])
                if "dimension" in c
                else derive_dimension(expectation_type=c["expectation_type"], kind=c["kind"])
            ),
            source_connection_id=source_id,
            # An imported check is a person's: it cannot inherit coverage settings (ADR 0047).
            config=coverage_settings_service.strip_flag(c["config"]),
            warn_threshold=c["warn_threshold"],
            fail_threshold=c["fail_threshold"],
            critical_threshold=c["critical_threshold"],
            # Document order: these rows share one `created_at`.
            ordinal=position,
            enabled=c.get("enabled", True),
        )
        for position, (c, source_id) in enumerate(zip(checks, source_ids, strict=True), start=1)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ClauseRef:
    """The contract clause a check enforces — `checks.contract_ref` (ADR 0052 §7)."""

    object: str
    field: str
    property: str | None = None
    rule_id: str | None = None

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "object": self.object,
            "property": self.property,
            "rule_id": self.rule_id,
            "field": self.field,
        }


@dataclass
class CheckDraft:
    """A check the importer will create, in `check_service.create_check`'s vocabulary."""

    name: str
    kind: str
    expectation_type: str
    config: dict[str, Any]
    ref: ClauseRef
    warn_threshold: Decimal | None = None
    fail_threshold: Decimal | None = None
    critical_threshold: Decimal | None = None
    dimension: str | None = None
    #: An explicit "leave unclassified" (ODCS `coverage`), which `dimension=None` cannot say.
    unclassified: bool = False
    engine: str = GX_ENGINE
    enabled: bool = True
    #: Declared `schema_drift` baseline columns (`type` None = not declared).
    baseline: list[dict[str, str | None]] | None = None
    #: A rule-level cron DataQ does not schedule, kept on the clause for the rollup.
    schedule: str | None = None
    #: `dataq.checkId` from an export — the existing check this draft stands for, if still there.
    adopt_check_id: str | None = None

    def fingerprint(self) -> str:
        """The rule's identity (type + config + thresholds), the `check_suggestions` idea."""
        return fingerprint(
            self.expectation_type,
            self.config,
            self.warn_threshold,
            self.fail_threshold,
            self.critical_threshold,
        )

    def ref_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        out = self.ref.as_dict()
        out["fingerprint"] = self.fingerprint()
        if self.schedule is not None:
            out["schedule"] = self.schedule
        return out


def fingerprint(
    expectation_type: str,
    config: dict[str, Any],
    warn: Decimal | None,
    fail: Decimal | None,
    critical: Decimal | None,
) -> str:
    canonical = json.dumps(
        {
            "type": expectation_type,
            "config": config,
            "thresholds": [None if t is None else str(Decimal(t)) for t in (warn, fail, critical)],
        },
        sort_keys=True,
        default=str,
    )
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode()).hexdigest()

def _validate_check(
    session: Session, connection: Connection, c: dict[str, Any]
) -> uuid.UUID | None:
    """One document check through the save-time gates check CRUD applies (kind +
    custom-SQL / monitor / comparison guardrails). Returns a comparison check's
    resolved source connection id.
    """
    validate_kind(c["kind"])
    # No Pydantic layer on the MCP door: a non-boolean would reach a NOT NULL boolean column.
    if not isinstance(c.get("enabled", True), bool):
        raise CheckConfigInvalidError("enabled must be true or false", detail={"field": "enabled"})
    # ADR 0036 §5: a document carrying a native-engine check imports only where the target
def _load_target_connection(session: Session, version: int, connection_id: uuid.UUID) -> Connection:
    if version != EXPORT_VERSION:
        raise SuiteImportInvalidError(
            f"unsupported export version {version!r}; this server imports v{EXPORT_VERSION}",
            detail={"version": version, "supported": EXPORT_VERSION},
        )
    connection = session.get(Connection, connection_id)
    if connection is None:
        raise SuiteImportConnectionInvalidError(
            "connection not found", detail={"connection_id": str(connection_id)}

"""Consumer-side data contracts (ADR 0052): import an ODCS v3 document, reconcile its suites.

A contract row is one VERSION of the document, stored verbatim. Importing it creates (or, for a
new version of a contract already linked to suites, reconciles) one suite per schema object on
the caller's connection, each carrying the checks the translation table produced. Every clause
ends in a check or in the contract's `unmapped` list — including a check the save-time
validators refuse, which is recorded with the validator's own message rather than failing the
whole import.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, selectinload

from backend.app.contracts import odcs
from backend.app.contracts import translate as tr
from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError
from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
from backend.app.datasources.monitors import SCHEMA_DRIFT
from backend.app.db.models import (
    CONTRACT_CHECK_ORIGIN,
    Check,
    Contract,
    Suite,
)
from backend.app.services import audit_service, suite_authz
from backend.app.services.check_dimension import derive_dimension
from backend.app.services.check_service import record_check_version
from backend.app.services.monitor_baseline import insert_baseline_if_absent
from backend.app.services.run_target import SuiteTargetInvalidError, validate_target
from backend.app.services.suite_io_service import (
    EXPORT_VERSION,
    _load_target_connection,
    _validate_check,
)

log = get_logger(__name__)


class ContractNotFoundError(DataQError):
    status_code = 404
    code = "contract_not_found"


class ContractVersionExistsError(DataQError):
    status_code = 409
    code = "contract_version_exists"


class ContractSuitesInvalidError(DataQError):
    status_code = 422
    code = "contract_suites_invalid"


@dataclass
class ImportOutcome:
    """What an import did — the REST/MCP response, and the audit payload's counts."""

    contract: Contract
    created_suite_ids: list[uuid.UUID] = field(default_factory=list)
    reconciled_suite_ids: list[uuid.UUID] = field(default_factory=list)
    #: Objects whose `physicalName` / `name` did not resolve to a run target on this connection:
    #: their suites exist (with checks) but cannot run until a target is set.
    untargeted_objects: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    checks_added: int = 0
    checks_updated: int = 0
    checks_disabled: int = 0
    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


# ───────────────────────────── targets ──────────────────────────────


def _target_for(connection_type: str, physical: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Map an ODCS `physicalName` (`table`, `schema.table`, `catalog.schema.table`, or a file
    path) onto this datasource's run-target shape, or `None` when it does not resolve."""
    parts = [p for p in physical.split(".") if p] if "/" not in physical else []
    target: dict[str, Any]
    if connection_type in {"adls_gen2", "s3", "gcs"}:
        target = {"path": physical}
    elif connection_type == "unity_catalog":
        if len(parts) != 3:
            return None
        target = {"catalog": parts[0], "schema": parts[1], "table": parts[2]}
    elif connection_type == "iceberg":
        if not parts:
            return None
        target = {"table": parts[-1]}
        if len(parts) > 1:
            target["namespace"] = ".".join(parts[:-1])
    else:
        if not parts or len(parts) > 2:
            return None
        target = {"table": parts[-1]}
        if len(parts) == 2:
            target["schema"] = parts[0]
    try:
        validate_target(connection_type, target)
    except SuiteTargetInvalidError:
        return None
    return target


# ───────────────────────────── checks ───────────────────────────────


def _document(draft: tr.CheckDraft) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The draft in the suite-document vocabulary `_validate_check` reads."""
    return {
        "name": draft.name,
        "kind": draft.kind,
        "engine": draft.engine,
        "expectation_type": draft.expectation_type,
        "config": draft.config,
        "warn_threshold": draft.warn_threshold,
        "fail_threshold": draft.fail_threshold,
        "critical_threshold": draft.critical_threshold,
        "enabled": draft.enabled,
        "dimension": _dimension(draft),
    }


def _dimension(draft: tr.CheckDraft) -> str | None:
    if draft.unclassified:
        return None
    if draft.dimension is not None:
        return draft.dimension
    return derive_dimension(expectation_type=draft.expectation_type, kind=draft.kind)


def _clause_key(ref: dict[str, Any] | None) -> tuple[Any, ...] | None:
    if not ref:
        return None
    return (ref.get("object"), ref.get("property"), ref.get("rule_id"), ref.get("field"))


def _current_fingerprint(check: Check) -> str:
    return tr.fingerprint(
        check.expectation_type,
        check.config,
        check.warn_threshold,
        check.fail_threshold,
        check.critical_threshold,
    )


def _apply(check: Check, draft: tr.CheckDraft) -> None:
    check.name = draft.name
    check.expectation_type = draft.expectation_type
    check.engine = draft.engine
    check.config = draft.config
    check.warn_threshold = draft.warn_threshold
    check.fail_threshold = draft.fail_threshold
    check.critical_threshold = draft.critical_threshold
    check.dimension = _dimension(draft)
    check.enabled = draft.enabled
    check.contract_ref = draft.ref_dict()


def _new_check(draft: tr.CheckDraft, ordinal: int) -> Check:
    check = Check(kind=draft.kind, origin=CONTRACT_CHECK_ORIGIN, ordinal=ordinal)
    _apply(check, draft)
    return check


def _seed_declared_baseline(session: Session, check: Check, draft: tr.CheckDraft) -> None:
    if draft.kind == SCHEMA_DRIFT and draft.baseline is not None:
        insert_baseline_if_absent(
            session,
            check_id=check.id,
            kind=SCHEMA_DRIFT,
            baseline={"columns": draft.baseline, "declared": True},
        )


def _accepted_drafts(
    session: Session, connection: Any, obj: tr.TranslatedObject
) -> tuple[list[tr.CheckDraft], list[tr.Unmapped]]:
    """The drafts the save-time validators accept; a refused one becomes an unmapped clause
    carrying the validator's message (ADR 0052 §3: the validator has the last word)."""
    accepted: list[tr.CheckDraft] = []
    refused: list[tr.Unmapped] = []
    for draft in obj.checks:
        try:
            _validate_check(session, connection, _document(draft))
        except DataQError as exc:
            refused.append(
                tr.Unmapped(
                    object=draft.ref.object,
                    property=draft.ref.property,
                    rule_id=draft.ref.rule_id,
                    field=draft.ref.field,
                    reason=f"DataQ refused the check this clause maps to: {exc}",
                    clause={"expectation_type": draft.expectation_type},
                )
            )
            continue
        accepted.append(draft)
    return accepted, refused


def _merge_pii(suite: Suite, columns: list[str]) -> None:
    if not columns:
        return
    policy = dict(suite.column_policy or {})
    existing = [str(c) for c in policy.get("pii_columns") or []]
    merged = existing + [c for c in columns if c.lower() not in {e.lower() for e in existing}]
    policy["pii_columns"] = merged
    suite.column_policy = policy


@dataclass
class _ReconcileCounts:
    added: int = 0
    updated: int = 0
    disabled: int = 0


def _reconcile(
    session: Session,
    suite: Suite,
    drafts: list[tr.CheckDraft],
    *,
    actor_id: uuid.UUID,
) -> tuple[_ReconcileCounts, list[tuple[Check, tr.CheckDraft]]]:
    """ADR 0052 §6 / ADR 0047's rules: add checks for new clauses, update a clause-derived check
    only if nobody edited it since its import, disable (never delete) the checks whose clause
    disappeared, and leave every hand-authored check alone."""
    counts = _ReconcileCounts()
    created: list[tuple[Check, tr.CheckDraft]] = []
    by_clause = {
        _clause_key(c.contract_ref): c
        for c in suite.checks
        if c.origin == CONTRACT_CHECK_ORIGIN and c.contract_ref
    }
    seen: set[tuple[Any, ...] | None] = set()
    next_ordinal = max((c.ordinal or 0 for c in suite.checks), default=0) + 1
    for draft in drafts:
        key = _clause_key(draft.ref.as_dict())
        seen.add(key)
        existing = by_clause.get(key)
        if existing is None:
            check = _new_check(draft, next_ordinal)
            next_ordinal += 1
            suite.checks.append(check)
            created.append((check, draft))
            counts.added += 1
            continue
        stored = (existing.contract_ref or {}).get("fingerprint")
        unedited = stored is not None and stored == _current_fingerprint(existing)
        if unedited and stored != draft.fingerprint():
            _apply(existing, draft)
            record_check_version(session, existing, actor_id=actor_id)
            counts.updated += 1
    for key, check in by_clause.items():
        if key not in seen and check.enabled:
            check.enabled = False
            record_check_version(session, check, actor_id=actor_id)
            counts.disabled += 1
    return counts, created


# ───────────────────────────── import ───────────────────────────────


def import_contract(
    session: Session,
    *,
    document: dict[str, Any] | None,
    document_yaml: str | None,
    connection_id: uuid.UUID,
    actor_id: uuid.UUID,
    suite_ids: list[uuid.UUID] | None = None,
    replace: bool = False,
) -> ImportOutcome:
    """Validate, translate and store an ODCS document, then create or reconcile its suites.

    - A version already stored is a 409 unless ``replace`` (then its stored spec is replaced
      and its linked suites reconciled).
    - A new version with ``suite_ids`` re-points those suites (each must be linked to an earlier
      version of the same contract) and reconciles them; without, it creates fresh suites.
    """
    raw = odcs.load_document(document=document, document_yaml=document_yaml)
    validated = odcs.validate_document(raw)
    connection = _load_target_connection(session, EXPORT_VERSION, connection_id)
    translated = tr.translate(validated.document, connection_type=connection.type)

    spec = validated.document
    odcs_id = str(spec["id"])
    version = str(spec["version"])
    existing = session.scalar(
        select(Contract).where(Contract.odcs_id == odcs_id, Contract.version == version)
    )
    if existing is not None and not replace:
        raise ContractVersionExistsError(
            "this contract version is already imported; import a new version, or send "
            "replace=true to replace it",
            detail={"contract_id": str(existing.id), "odcs_id": odcs_id, "version": version},
        )

    if existing is not None:
        contract = existing
        targets = list(contract.suites)
    else:
        contract = Contract(odcs_id=odcs_id, version=version, created_by=actor_id)
        session.add(contract)
        targets = _suites_to_repoint(session, odcs_id, suite_ids or [], actor_id=actor_id)

    contract.name = str(spec.get("name") or odcs_id)[:256]
    contract.status = str(spec["status"])[:32] if spec.get("status") is not None else None
    contract.domain = str(spec["domain"])[:256] if spec.get("domain") is not None else None
    contract.tenant = str(spec["tenant"])[:256] if spec.get("tenant") is not None else None
    contract.api_version = str(spec["apiVersion"])
    contract.spec = spec
    session.flush()

    outcome = ImportOutcome(contract=contract, warnings=list(validated.warnings))
    unmapped: list[tr.Unmapped] = list(translated.unmapped)
    by_object = {s.contract_object: s for s in targets}
    new_checks: list[tuple[Check, tr.CheckDraft]] = []

    for obj in translated.objects:
        drafts, refused = _accepted_drafts(session, connection, obj)
        unmapped.extend(refused)
        suite = by_object.get(obj.name)
        if suite is None:
            target = _target_for(connection.type, obj.physical_name)
            if target is None:
                outcome.untargeted_objects.append(obj.name)
            suite = Suite(
                name=f"{contract.name} · {obj.name}"[:128],
                description=f"Enforces data contract {contract.name} {version}"[:1024],
                connection_id=connection.id,
                target=target,
                created_by=actor_id,
                contract_id=contract.id,
                contract_object=obj.name,
            )
            suite.checks = []
            session.add(suite)
            for ordinal, draft in enumerate(drafts, start=1):
                check = _new_check(draft, ordinal)
                suite.checks.append(check)
                new_checks.append((check, draft))
            outcome.checks_added += len(drafts)
            _merge_pii(suite, obj.pii_columns)
            session.flush()
            outcome.created_suite_ids.append(suite.id)
        else:
            suite.contract_id = contract.id
            suite.contract_object = obj.name
            counts, created = _reconcile(session, suite, drafts, actor_id=actor_id)
            new_checks.extend(created)
            outcome.checks_added += counts.added
            outcome.checks_updated += counts.updated
            outcome.checks_disabled += counts.disabled
            _merge_pii(suite, obj.pii_columns)
            session.flush()
            outcome.reconciled_suite_ids.append(suite.id)
        if obj.schedule_cron:
            _ensure_schedule(session, suite, obj, actor_id=actor_id, unmapped=unmapped)

    session.flush()
    for check, draft in new_checks:
        record_check_version(session, check, actor_id=actor_id)
        _seed_declared_baseline(session, check, draft)
    contract.unmapped = [u.as_dict() for u in unmapped]

    audit_service.record(
        session,
        action="contract.import",
        entity_type="contract",
        entity_id=contract.id,
        actor=actor_id,
        after={
            "id": str(contract.id),
            "odcs_id": odcs_id,
            "version": version,
            "replaced": existing is not None,
            "suites_created": len(outcome.created_suite_ids),
            "suites_reconciled": len(outcome.reconciled_suite_ids),
            "checks_added": outcome.checks_added,
            "checks_updated": outcome.checks_updated,
            "checks_disabled": outcome.checks_disabled,
            "unmapped": len(unmapped),
        },
    )
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(contract)
    log.info(
        "contract_imported",
        contract_id=str(contract.id),
        suites_created=len(outcome.created_suite_ids),
        suites_reconciled=len(outcome.reconciled_suite_ids),
        unmapped=len(unmapped),
    )
    return outcome


def _suites_to_repoint(
    session: Session, odcs_id: str, suite_ids: list[uuid.UUID], *, actor_id: uuid.UUID
) -> list[Suite]:
    """The suites a new version takes over: each `edit`-able and linked to an earlier version
    of the SAME contract (422 otherwise — re-pointing a stranger's suite is not an import)."""
    suites: list[Suite] = []
    for suite_id in dict.fromkeys(suite_ids):
        suite = suite_authz.require_permission(session, suite_id, actor_id, minimum="edit")
        linked = session.get(Contract, suite.contract_id) if suite.contract_id else None
        if linked is None or linked.odcs_id != odcs_id:
            raise ContractSuitesInvalidError(
                "a suite named in suite_ids is not linked to an earlier version of this contract",
                detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id)},
            )
        suites.append(suite)
    return suites


def _ensure_schedule(
    session: Session,
    suite: Suite,
    obj: tr.TranslatedObject,
    *,
    actor_id: uuid.UUID,
    unmapped: list[tr.Unmapped],
) -> None:
    """The object's `dataq.schedule` cron — created once; an existing schedule on the suite is
    left alone (a person may have tuned it). A cron the scheduler refuses is unmapped."""
    from backend.app.db.models import Schedule
    from backend.app.services import cron

    if session.scalar(select(Schedule.id).where(Schedule.suite_id == suite.id).limit(1)):
        return
    try:
        next_run_at = cron.next_fire(obj.schedule_cron or "", obj.schedule_timezone)
    except DataQError as exc:
        unmapped.append(
            tr.Unmapped(
                object=obj.name,
                field="customProperties.dataq.schedule",
                reason=f"the scheduler refused this cron: {exc}",
                clause={"schedule": obj.schedule_cron},
            )
        )
        return
    session.add(
        Schedule(
            suite_id=suite.id,
            cron_expr=obj.schedule_cron,
            timezone=obj.schedule_timezone,
            enabled=True,
            next_run_at=next_run_at,
            created_by=actor_id,
        )
    )


# ───────────────────────────── reads ────────────────────────────────


@dataclass
class VisibleContract:
    contract: Contract
    suites: list[Suite]
    restricted_suite_count: int


def _visible(session: Session, contract: Contract, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> VisibleContract | None:
    """A contract is visible when the caller can `view` at least one linked suite, or is a
    workspace admin (who also sees a contract with no linked suite)."""
    suites = list(contract.suites)
    perms = suite_authz.effective_permissions(session, suites, user_id)
    visible = [s for s in suites if perms.get(s.id) is not None]
    is_admin = suite_authz.is_workspace_admin(session, user_id)
    if not visible and not is_admin:
        return None
    return VisibleContract(contract, visible, len(suites) - len(visible))


def list_contracts(session: Session, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> list[VisibleContract]:
    rows = session.scalars(
        select(Contract)
        .options(selectinload(Contract.suites))
        .order_by(Contract.name, Contract.version)
    )
    return [v for c in rows if (v := _visible(session, c, user_id)) is not None]


def get_contract(session: Session, contract_id: uuid.UUID, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> VisibleContract:
    """404 — never 403 — for a contract the caller cannot see (ADR 0027's no-leak rule)."""
    contract = session.get(Contract, contract_id)
    visible = _visible(session, contract, user_id) if contract is not None else None
    if visible is None:
        raise ContractNotFoundError(
            "contract not found", detail={"contract_id": str(contract_id)}
        )
    return visible


def delete_contract(session: Session, contract_id: uuid.UUID, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> None:
    """Unlink the contract's suites (both columns, together) and delete the row; suites, checks
    and results stay. Requires `edit` on every linked suite — unlinking is a suite mutation."""
    visible = get_contract(session, contract_id, user_id)
    for suite in visible.contract.suites:
        suite_authz.require_permission(session, suite.id, user_id, minimum="edit")
    for suite in visible.contract.suites:
        suite.contract_id = None
        suite.contract_object = None
    audit_service.record(
        session,
        action="contract.delete",
        entity_type="contract",
        entity_id=visible.contract.id,
        actor=user_id,
        before={
            "id": str(visible.contract.id),
            "odcs_id": visible.contract.odcs_id,
            "version": visible.contract.version,
            "suites_unlinked": len(visible.contract.suites),
        },
    )
    session.delete(visible.contract)
    session.commit()

"""A contract + its linked suites' current checks → an ODCS v3 document (ADR 0052 §4).

The stored spec is the base, so every field the producer wrote survives. DataQ-only facts ride in
`customProperties` with a `dataq.` prefix: on the document (`exportedAt`), on each schema object
backed by a suite (`suiteId`, `connectionType`), and on each quality rule a check enforces
(`checkId`, `kind`, `engine`, thresholds, `enabled`). A check with no ODCS-native shape — one a
person added to the suite, or any kind the table cannot express — is appended to its object as a
`type: custom, engine: dataq` rule whose `implementation` is the suite-document check, so
importing the export recreates every check.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from backend.app.contracts import odcs
from backend.app.contracts import translate as tr
from backend.app.db.models import CHECK_ORDER, CONTRACT_CHECK_ORIGIN, Check, Connection, Contract, Suite
from backend.app.services.suite_io_service import export_suite

_PREFIX = f"{tr.DATAQ_VENDOR}."


def _json_safe(value: Any) -> Any:
    """Thresholds are NUMERIC (`Decimal`); a YAML/JSON document wants plain numbers or strings."""
    return json.loads(json.dumps(value, default=lambda v: str(v) if isinstance(v, Decimal) else v))


def _set_custom(node: dict[str, Any], name: str, value: Any) -> None:
    """Replace any earlier `dataq.<name>` entry (an export of an export stays single-valued)."""
    key = f"{_PREFIX}{name}"
    kept = [
        item
        for item in node.get("customProperties") or []
        if not (isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("property") in {key, name}
                and (item.get("property") == key or item.get("vendor") == tr.DATAQ_VENDOR))
    ]
    kept.append({"property": key, "value": _json_safe(value)})
    node["customProperties"] = kept


def _find_rule(obj: dict[str, Any], ref: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """The quality rule a check's clause names, by the same `(property, rule_id)` the importer
    recorded (`rule.id`, else `quality[<index>]`)."""
    prop_name = ref.get("property")
    if prop_name is None:
        container = obj
    else:
        container = next(
            (
                p
                for p in obj.get("properties") or ()
                if isinstance(p, dict) and tr._column_name(p) == prop_name
            ),
            None,
        )
        if container is None:
            return None
    for index, rule in enumerate(container.get("quality") or ()):
        if isinstance(rule, dict) and tr._rule_id(rule, index) == ref.get("rule_id"):
            return rule
    return None


def _annotate_rule(rule: dict[str, Any], check: Check) -> None:
    _set_custom(rule, "checkId", str(check.id))
    _set_custom(rule, "kind", check.kind)
    _set_custom(rule, "engine", check.engine)
    for name, value in (
        ("warnThreshold", check.warn_threshold),
        ("failThreshold", check.fail_threshold),
        ("criticalThreshold", check.critical_threshold),
    ):
        if value is not None:
            _set_custom(rule, name, value)
    _set_custom(rule, "enabled", check.enabled)


def _native_rule(check: Check, document: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "type": "custom",
        "engine": tr.DATAQ_VENDOR,
        "name": check.name,
        "implementation": _json_safe(document),
        "customProperties": [{"property": f"{_PREFIX}checkId", "value": str(check.id)}],
    }


def export_contract(session: Session, contract: Contract, suites: list[Suite]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The ODCS document for ``contract`` as enforced by ``suites`` (the caller's visible ones,
    already authorised). Written in the newest vendored v3 vocabulary."""
    doc = tr.normalize_document(contract.spec)
    doc["apiVersion"] = odcs.NEWEST_VERSION
    _set_custom(doc, "exportedAt", datetime.now(UTC).isoformat())
    objects = {
        o.get("name"): o for o in doc.get("schema") or () if isinstance(o, dict)
    }
    for suite in suites:
        obj = objects.get(suite.contract_object)
        if obj is None:
            continue
        connection = session.get(Connection, suite.connection_id)
        _set_custom(obj, "suiteId", str(suite.id))
        if connection is not None:
            _set_custom(obj, "connectionType", connection.type)
        checks = list(
            session.scalars(select(Check).where(Check.suite_id == suite.id).order_by(*CHECK_ORDER))
        )
        documents = export_suite(session, suite)["checks"]
        for check, document in zip(checks, documents, strict=True):
            ref = check.contract_ref if check.origin == CONTRACT_CHECK_ORIGIN else None
            if ref is not None:
                rule = _find_rule(obj, ref) if ref.get("rule_id") else None
                if rule is not None:
                    _annotate_rule(rule, check)
                # A schema-field clause (required, unique, …) is already in the document.
                if rule is not None or not ref.get("rule_id"):
                    continue
            obj.setdefault("quality", []).append(_native_rule(check, document))

"""contract_service + the ODCS export against a real Postgres (ADR 0052)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import json
import uuid
from typing import Any

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import select

from backend.app.contracts import odcs
from backend.app.contracts import translate as tr
from backend.app.contracts.export import export_contract
from backend.app.db.models import (
    AuditEvent,
    Check,
    CheckVersion,
    Connection,
    Contract,
    MonitorBaseline,
    Schedule,
    Suite,
    SuiteShare,
    User,
)
from backend.app.services import contract_service as svc
from backend.app.services.schema_drift import diff_schemas


def _user(db: Any, role: str = "member") -> User:
    u = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f"u-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@ex", role=role)
    db.add(u)
    db.flush()
    return u


def _connection(db: Any, owner: User, type_: str = "snowflake") -> Connection:
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"c-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        type=type_,
        env="dev",
        config={"account": "ab12345", "database": "ANALYTICS", "warehouse": "WH"},
        secret_ref="kv-x",
        created_by=owner.id,
    )
    db.add(conn)
    db.flush()
    return conn


def _doc(version: str = "1.0.0", **overrides: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    doc: dict[str, Any] = {
        "apiVersion": "v3.2.0",
        "kind": "DataContract",
        "id": "seller-payments",
        "name": "seller_payments",
        "version": version,
        "status": "active",
        "domain": "seller",
        "schema": [
            {
                "name": "orders",
                "physicalName": "FINANCE.ORDERS",
                "properties": [
                    {"name": "order_id", "logicalType": "integer", "required": True, "unique": True},
                    {"name": "email", "logicalType": "string", "classification": "confidential"},
                    {
                        "name": "amount",
                        "logicalType": "number",
                        "quality": [
                            {"id": "amount-nulls", "metric": "nullValues", "mustBe": 0},
                        ],
                    },
                ],
                "quality": [{"id": "row-floor", "metric": "rowCount", "mustBeGreaterThan": 10}],
                "customProperties": [{"property": "dataq.schedule", "value": "0 2 * * *"}],
            },
            {"name": "refunds", "physicalName": "FINANCE.REFUNDS", "properties": [{"name": "id"}]},
        ],
        "slaProperties": [{"property": "retention", "value": 7, "unit": "y"}],
    }
    doc.update(overrides)
    return doc


def _import(db: Any, actor: User, conn: Connection, doc: dict[str, Any], **kw: Any) -> svc.ImportOutcome:
    return svc.import_contract(
        db, document=doc, document_yaml=None, connection_id=conn.id, actor_id=actor.id, **kw
    )


def _suite(db: Any, outcome: svc.ImportOutcome, obj: str) -> Suite:
    suite = db.scalar(
        select(Suite).where(
            Suite.contract_id == outcome.contract.id, Suite.contract_object == obj
        )
    )
    assert suite is not None
    return suite


# ───────────────────────────── import ───────────────────────────────


def test_a_fresh_import_creates_one_suite_per_schema_object(db_session: Any) -> None:
    actor = _user(db_session)
    conn = _connection(db_session, actor)
    outcome = _import(db_session, actor, conn, _doc())

    contract = outcome.contract
    assert (contract.odcs_id, contract.version, contract.name, contract.domain) == (
        "seller-payments",
        "1.0.0",
        "seller_payments",
        "seller",
    )
    assert contract.spec["schema"][0]["name"] == "orders"  # stored verbatim
    assert len(outcome.created_suite_ids) == 2 and outcome.untargeted_objects == []

    orders = _suite(db_session, outcome, "orders")
    assert orders.target == {"schema": "FINANCE", "table": "ORDERS"}
    assert orders.column_policy == {"pii_columns": ["email"]}
    kinds = sorted(c.expectation_type for c in orders.checks)
    assert kinds == sorted(
        [
            "expect_column_values_to_not_be_null",  # order_id required
            "expect_column_values_to_be_unique",
            "expect_column_values_to_not_be_null",  # amount nulls rule
            "monitor:schema_drift",
            "monitor:volume",
        ]
    )
    assert all(c.origin == "contract" and c.contract_ref for c in orders.checks)
    # Every created check has its v1 snapshot.
    versions = db_session.scalars(
        select(CheckVersion).where(CheckVersion.check_id.in_([c.id for c in orders.checks]))
    ).all()
    assert len(versions) == len(orders.checks)
    # The schedule from customProperties.
    schedule = db_session.scalar(select(Schedule).where(Schedule.suite_id == orders.id))
    assert schedule is not None and schedule.cron == "0 2 * * *"
    # The declared schema-drift baseline is seeded, not learned.
    drift = next(c for c in orders.checks if c.expectation_type == "monitor:schema_drift")
    baseline = db_session.scalar(select(MonitorBaseline).where(MonitorBaseline.check_id == drift.id))
    assert baseline is not None and baseline.baseline["declared"] is True
    assert [c["name"] for c in baseline.baseline["columns"]] == ["order_id", "email", "amount"]
    # Not-enforced clauses are stored, with the reason.
    assert [u["field"] for u in contract.unmapped] == ["slaProperties.retention"]


def test_the_import_is_audited_with_counts_never_the_document(db_session: Any) -> None:
    actor = _user(db_session)
    conn = _connection(db_session, actor)
    outcome = _import(db_session, actor, conn, _doc())
    event = db_session.scalar(
        select(AuditEvent).where(
            AuditEvent.action == "contract.import", AuditEvent.entity_id == outcome.contract.id
        )
    )
    assert event is not None
    assert event.after["suites_created"] == 2 and event.after["unmapped"] == 1
    assert "FINANCE.ORDERS" not in json.dumps(event.after)
    assert "schema" not in event.after


def test_an_unresolvable_physical_name_leaves_the_suite_untargeted_and_says_so(
    db_session: Any,
) -> None:
    actor = _user(db_session)
    conn = _connection(db_session, actor)
    doc = _doc()
    doc["schema"][1]["physicalName"] = "a.b.c.d"
    outcome = _import(db_session, actor, conn, doc)
    assert outcome.untargeted_objects == ["refunds"]
    assert _suite(db_session, outcome, "refunds").target is None


def test_a_check_the_validators_refuse_becomes_an_unmapped_clause(db_session: Any) -> None:
    actor = _user(db_session)
    conn = _connection(db_session, actor)
    doc = _doc()
    # A negative row ceiling is a volume config the save-time validator refuses.
    doc["schema"][0]["quality"] = [{"id": "bad", "metric": "rowCount", "mustBeLessThan": 0}]
    outcome = _import(db_session, actor, conn, doc)
    reasons = [u for u in outcome.contract.unmapped if u.get("rule_id") == "bad"]
    assert len(reasons) == 1 and reasons[0]["reason"].startswith("DataQ refused")
    orders = _suite(db_session, outcome, "orders")
    assert "monitor:volume" not in {c.expectation_type for c in orders.checks}


def test_the_same_version_is_refused_unless_replace(db_session: Any) -> None:
    actor = _user(db_session)
    conn = _connection(db_session, actor)
    first = _import(db_session, actor, conn, _doc())
    with pytest.raises(svc.ContractVersionExistsError):
        _import(db_session, actor, conn, _doc())
    again = _import(db_session, actor, conn, _doc(), replace=True)
    assert again.contract.id == first.contract.id
    assert again.created_suite_ids == [] and len(again.reconciled_suite_ids) == 2
    assert (again.checks_added, again.checks_updated, again.checks_disabled) == (0, 0, 0)


def test_a_new_version_reconciles_the_suites_it_takes_over(db_session: Any) -> None:
    actor = _user(db_session)
    conn = _connection(db_session, actor)
    first = _import(db_session, actor, conn, _doc())
    orders = _suite(db_session, first, "orders")
    by_rule = {(c.contract_ref or {}).get("rule_id"): c for c in orders.checks}

    # A person edits the row-floor check; and adds their own check to the suite.
    edited = by_rule["row-floor"]
    edited.config = {"min_rows": 50}
    hand = Check(
        suite_id=orders.id,
        name="mine",
        kind="expectation",
        expectation_type="expect_column_values_to_not_be_null",
        config={"column": "email"},
        ordinal=99,
    )
    db_session.add(hand)
    db_session.commit()

    v2 = copy.deepcopy(_doc("2.0.0"))
    v2["schema"][0]["quality"] = [{"id": "row-floor", "metric": "rowCount", "mustBeGreaterThan": 99}]
    v2["schema"][0]["properties"][2]["quality"] = [
        {"id": "amount-nulls", "metric": "nullValues", "mustBeLessThan": 5, "unit": "percent"}
    ]
    v2["schema"][0]["properties"].append({"name": "currency", "required": True})
    del v2["schema"][0]["properties"][0]["unique"]  # the unique clause disappears

    suite_ids = [s for s in first.created_suite_ids]
    second = _import(db_session, actor, conn, v2, suite_ids=suite_ids)
    assert second.contract.id != first.contract.id
    assert sorted(second.reconciled_suite_ids) == sorted(suite_ids)
    db_session.refresh(orders)
    checks = {c.id: c for c in orders.checks}

    assert checks[edited.id].config == {"min_rows": 50}  # a person's edit survives
    assert checks[hand.id].enabled and checks[hand.id].origin == "user"  # untouched
    nulls = next(
        c for c in checks.values() if (c.contract_ref or {}).get("rule_id") == "amount-nulls"
    )
    assert nulls.fail_threshold == 5  # unedited → updated to the new clause
    unique = next(
        c for c in checks.values() if c.expectation_type == "expect_column_values_to_be_unique"
    )
    assert unique.enabled is False  # disabled, never deleted
    assert any(
        (c.contract_ref or {}).get("property") == "currency" for c in checks.values()
    )  # added
    assert orders.contract_id == second.contract.id
    assert (second.checks_added, second.checks_updated, second.checks_disabled) == (1, 1, 1)


def test_a_suite_from_another_contract_cannot_be_taken_over(db_session: Any) -> None:
    actor = _user(db_session)
    conn = _connection(db_session, actor)
    other = _import(db_session, actor, conn, _doc(id="other-contract"))
    with pytest.raises(svc.ContractSuitesInvalidError):
        _import(db_session, actor, conn, _doc("2.0.0"), suite_ids=other.created_suite_ids[:1])

    """Percent the row count falls **outside** the band (0 in range); a missing bound is open."""
    if min_rows is not None and row_count < min_rows:
        return (min_rows - row_count) / min_rows * 100.0 if min_rows else 100.0
    if max_rows is not None and row_count > max_rows:
        return (row_count - max_rows) / max_rows * 100.0 if max_rows else 100.0
    return 0.0


def _volume_bound(config: dict[str, Any], key: str) -> int | None:
    if key not in config or config[key] is None:
        return None
    value = config[key]
    # bool is an int subclass: `{"min_rows": true}` must not pass as 1.
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        raise MonitorConfigError(f"volume {key} must be a whole number, not {value!r}")
    try:
        number = int(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise MonitorConfigError(f"volume {key} must be a whole number: {_echo(config)}") from exc
    if number != value and not (isinstance(value, str) and value.strip() == str(number)):
        raise MonitorConfigError(f"volume {key} must be a whole number: {_echo(config)}")
    if number < 0:
        raise MonitorConfigError(f"volume {key} must be 0 or more: {_echo(config)}")
    return number

    return min_rows, max_rows

"""Consumer-side data contracts (ADR 0052): ODCS v3 import, reads, ODCS export, unlink-delete."""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Annotated, Any

import yaml
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Response, status
from pydantic import Field, model_validator
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from backend.app.api.v1._base import ApiModel, ApiRequestModel
from backend.app.contracts.export import export_contract
from backend.app.core.auth import MemberUser, get_current_user
from backend.app.db.models import User
from backend.app.db.session import get_db
from backend.app.services import contract_service as svc

router = APIRouter(tags=["contracts"])

#: The largest ODCS document accepted as YAML text — the suite-document cap's order of magnitude.
MAX_CONTRACT_YAML_CHARS = 1_000_000


class ContractImportRequest(ApiRequestModel):
    """An ODCS v3 document as JSON (`document`) or YAML text (`document_yaml`) — exactly one."""

    connection_id: uuid.UUID = Field(
        description="The connection the contract's suites run on (one suite per schema object)."
    )
    document: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    document_yaml: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=MAX_CONTRACT_YAML_CHARS)
    suite_ids: list[uuid.UUID] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        max_length=200,
        description=(
            "For a NEW version: the suites linked to an earlier version of this contract that "
            "this version takes over and reconciles. Omit to create fresh suites."
        ),
    )
    replace: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description="Replace an already-imported version (and reconcile its linked suites).",
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _exactly_one_document(self) -> ContractImportRequest:
        if (self.document is None) == (self.document_yaml is None):
            raise ValueError("send exactly one of document or document_yaml")
        return self


class ContractSuiteRead(ApiModel):
    id: uuid.UUID
    name: str
    #: The ODCS schema object this suite enforces.
    contract_object: str | None
    #: False when the object's `physicalName` did not resolve to a run target: the suite holds
    #: its checks but cannot run until a target is set.
    runnable: bool


class UnmappedClauseRead(ApiModel):
    """A clause no DataQ check enforces, and why — shown as *not enforced*, never dropped."""

    object: str | None
    property: str | None
    rule_id: str | None
    field: str
    reason: str
    clause: dict[str, Any]


class ContractRead(ApiModel):
    id: uuid.UUID
    #: The document's own `id` — the identity across versions and renames.
    odcs_id: str
    name: str
    version: str
    status: str | None
    domain: str | None
    tenant: str | None
    #: The `apiVersion` the document declared.
    api_version: str
    created_at: datetime
    #: Linked suites the caller can view.
    suites: list[ContractSuiteRead]
    #: Linked suites the caller cannot view — counted, never named (ADR 0037).
    restricted_suite_count: int
    unmapped: list[UnmappedClauseRead]

    @classmethod

"""REST surface for data contracts (ADR 0052): import, reads, export, delete, authz."""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator
from typing import Any

import pytest
import yaml
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from backend.app.db.models import Connection, Share, User
from backend.app.db.session import get_db
from backend.app.main import app
from backend.tests.support.fake_secret_store import FakeSecretStore, override_secret_store

AsRole = Callable[..., tuple[Any, dict[str, str]]]


@pytest.fixture
def client(db_session: Any) -> Iterator[TestClient]:
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session
    override_secret_store(app, FakeSecretStore())
    try:
        yield TestClient(app)
    finally:
        app.dependency_overrides.clear()


def _connection(db: Any, owner: User) -> Connection:
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"pg-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        type="postgres",
        env="dev",
        config={"host": "db.example.com", "database": "analytics"},
        secret_ref="kv-pg",
        created_by=owner.id,
    )
    db.add(conn)
    db.commit()
    return conn


_DOC_YAML = """
apiVersion: v3.2.0
kind: DataContract
id: orders-contract
name: orders
version: 1.0.0
status: active
schema:
  - name: orders
    physicalName: public.orders
    properties:
      - name: order_id
        logicalType: integer
        required: true
      - name: email
        logicalType: string
        classification: restricted
    quality:
      - id: floor
        metric: rowCount
        mustBeGreaterThan: 0
slaProperties:
  - property: retention
    value: 7
    unit: y
"""


def _import(client: TestClient, headers: dict[str, str], conn: Connection, **body: Any) -> Any:
    payload: dict[str, Any] = {"connection_id": str(conn.id), "document_yaml": _DOC_YAML}
    payload.update(body)
    return client.post("/api/v1/contracts/import", json=payload, headers=headers)


def test_import_returns_the_contract_suites_and_unmapped_clauses(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Any, as_role: AsRole
) -> None:
    member, headers = as_role("member")
    conn = _connection(db_session, member)
    resp = _import(client, headers, conn)
    assert resp.status_code == 201, resp.text
    body = resp.json()
    contract = body["contract"]
    assert (contract["odcs_id"], contract["version"], contract["api_version"]) == (
        "orders-contract",
        "1.0.0",
        "v3.2.0",
    )
    assert len(body["created_suite_ids"]) == 1 and body["untargeted_objects"] == []
    assert contract["suites"][0]["runnable"] is True
    assert [u["field"] for u in contract["unmapped"]] == ["slaProperties.retention"]
    assert body["checks_added"] == 3  # required, schema drift, volume


def test_a_viewer_cannot_import(client: TestClient, db_session: Any, as_role: AsRole) -> None:
    viewer, headers = as_role("viewer")
    conn = _connection(db_session, viewer)
    assert _import(client, headers, conn).status_code == 403


def test_an_invalid_document_is_a_422_naming_where(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Any, as_role: AsRole
) -> None:
    member, headers = as_role("member")
    conn = _connection(db_session, member)
    resp = _import(client, headers, conn, document_yaml="apiVersion: v3.2.0\nkind: DataContract\n")
    assert resp.status_code == 422
    assert "id" in resp.json()["error"]["message"]


def test_v2_and_v4_documents_are_refused(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Any, as_role: AsRole
) -> None:
    member, headers = as_role("member")
    conn = _connection(db_session, member)
    for api in ("v2.2.2", "v4.0.0"):
        resp = _import(client, headers, conn, document_yaml=_DOC_YAML.replace("v3.2.0", api))
        assert resp.status_code == 422, api


def test_send_exactly_one_document(client: TestClient, db_session: Any, as_role: AsRole) -> None:
    member, headers = as_role("member")
    conn = _connection(db_session, member)
    resp = client.post(
        "/api/v1/contracts/import", json={"connection_id": str(conn.id)}, headers=headers
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 422


def test_reimporting_the_same_version_is_a_409(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Any, as_role: AsRole
) -> None:
    member, headers = as_role("member")
    conn = _connection(db_session, member)
    assert _import(client, headers, conn).status_code == 201
    again = _import(client, headers, conn)
    assert again.status_code == 409
    assert again.json()["error"]["code"] == "contract_version_exists"


def test_reads_are_scoped_to_suites_the_caller_can_see(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Any, as_role: AsRole
) -> None:
    owner, owner_headers = as_role("member")
    conn = _connection(db_session, owner)
    contract_id = _import(client, owner_headers, conn).json()["contract"]["id"]
    _, stranger_headers = as_role("member")

    listed = client.get("/api/v1/contracts", headers=owner_headers)
    assert [c["id"] for c in listed.json()] == [contract_id]
    stranger_list = client.get("/api/v1/contracts", headers=stranger_headers)
    assert stranger_list.json() == []
    hidden = client.get(f"/api/v1/contracts/{contract_id}", headers=stranger_headers)
    assert hidden.status_code == 404


def test_a_view_share_sees_the_contract_but_cannot_delete_it(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Any, as_role: AsRole
) -> None:
    owner, owner_headers = as_role("member")
    conn = _connection(db_session, owner)
    body = _import(client, owner_headers, conn).json()
    viewer, viewer_headers = as_role("member")
    db_session.add(
        Share(suite_id=uuid.UUID(body["created_suite_ids"][0]), user_id=viewer.id, permission="view")
    )
    db_session.commit()
    contract_id = body["contract"]["id"]
    seen = client.get(f"/api/v1/contracts/{contract_id}", headers=viewer_headers)
    assert seen.status_code == 200
    denied = client.delete(f"/api/v1/contracts/{contract_id}", headers=viewer_headers)
    assert denied.status_code == 403


def test_export_is_a_valid_odcs_document_in_json_and_yaml(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Any, as_role: AsRole
) -> None:
    member, headers = as_role("member")
    conn = _connection(db_session, member)
    contract_id = _import(client, headers, conn).json()["contract"]["id"]

    as_json = client.get(f"/api/v1/contracts/{contract_id}/export", headers=headers)
    assert as_json.status_code == 200
    document = as_json.json()
    assert document["apiVersion"] == "v3.2.0" and document["id"] == "orders-contract"
    as_yaml = client.get(f"/api/v1/contracts/{contract_id}/export?format=yaml", headers=headers)
    assert as_yaml.headers["content-type"].startswith("application/yaml")
    assert yaml.safe_load(as_yaml.text)["id"] == "orders-contract"


def test_delete_unlinks_and_keeps_the_suites(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Any, as_role: AsRole
) -> None:
    member, headers = as_role("member")
    conn = _connection(db_session, member)
    body = _import(client, headers, conn).json()
    contract_id = body["contract"]["id"]
    deleted = client.delete(f"/api/v1/contracts/{contract_id}", headers=headers)
    assert deleted.status_code == 204
    gone = client.get(f"/api/v1/contracts/{contract_id}", headers=headers)
    assert gone.status_code == 404
    suite = client.get(f"/api/v1/suites/{body['created_suite_ids'][0]}", headers=headers)
    assert suite.status_code == 200

# Data contracts (ODCS)

A data contract is a team's written promise about a dataset: its columns, the quality rules it
keeps and how fresh it stays. DataQ reads contracts in the
[Open Data Contract Standard](https://bitol-io.github.io/open-data-contract-standard/) (ODCS) v3
and turns them into ordinary suites and checks that run, alert and score like any other. This is
the **consumer** side: DataQ checks data that has already landed against the contract. It does not
enforce anything inside the producer's pipeline.

## Import a contract

Send the ODCS document, as YAML text or JSON, with the connection the data lives on:

```bash
curl -X POST "$DATAQ/api/v1/contracts/import" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DATAQ_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$(jq -n --arg yaml "$(cat orders.odcs.yaml)" --arg conn "$CONNECTION_ID" \
        '{connection_id: $conn, document_yaml: $yaml}')"
```

DataQ validates the document against the ODCS JSON Schema for its `apiVersion` (v3.0.0 to
v3.2.0; a newer v3 minor is accepted with a warning; v2 and v4 are refused), stores it exactly as
sent, and creates **one suite per schema object**, targeted at the object's `physicalName`
(`schema.table`, `catalog.schema.table` on Unity Catalog, a path on object stores). The response
lists the suites it created, any object whose name did not resolve to a table on that connection
(its suite exists but cannot run until you set a target), and every clause it could not enforce.

Importing requires the Member role. Each version of a contract is stored once; importing the same
`id` and `version` again is refused unless you send `replace: true`.

## What becomes a check

| In the contract | In DataQ |
|---|---|
| `required: true` | not-null check |
| `unique: true`, a single `primaryKey` | uniqueness check |
| several `primaryKey` properties | compound uniqueness |
| `logicalTypeOptions` minimum / maximum (exclusive too), length, pattern | range, length and regex checks |
| `enum` / `invalidValues` with `validValues` or `pattern` | value-set or regex check |
| `nullValues`, `missingValues`, `duplicateValues` | not-null, not-in-set, uniqueness checks; a `percent` bound becomes the fail threshold |
| `rowCount` | a volume monitor; a one-sided bound stays one-sided |
| the object's property list | a schema-drift check whose baseline is the declared columns |
| `type: sql` rules | a custom SQL check that fails when the query's result breaks the operator, or is empty |
| `type: custom` with `engine: great-expectations` | that expectation, if DataQ allows it |
| `slaProperties` `latency` on a timestamp column | a freshness monitor |
| `classification` of `confidential`, `restricted`, `pii`, `sensitive` or `secret` | the column joins the suite's PII columns, so failing samples mask it |
| `severity` `info` / `warning` / `error` / `critical` | warn / warn / fail / critical; no severity means fail |
| `dimension` | DataQ's dimension (`conformity` reads as validity; `coverage` stays unclassified) |

A schedule for an object's suite comes from a `dataq.schedule` cron in the object's
`customProperties`, and `dataq.maxAgeHours` (with `dataq.freshnessColumn`) adds a freshness
ceiling.

### Not enforced

Everything else is kept on the contract as **not enforced**, with the reason, and never silently
dropped. That includes `frequency` (a refresh cadence is not a staleness limit; state the limit as
`latency`), `retention` and the other service-level properties, `text` rules, rules for another
engine such as Soda, a `rows` bound on `nullValues`, `multipleOf`, and any check DataQ's own
validators refuse for that datasource.

## A new version

Import the new version with `suite_ids` set to the suites the old version created. DataQ re-points
them and reconciles their checks: clauses that are new get a check, a check nobody has edited since
the import is updated to the new clause, a check whose clause disappeared is **switched off** (not
deleted, so its history stays), and checks people added to the suite themselves are left alone.
Without `suite_ids`, the new version creates fresh suites.

## Export

`GET /api/v1/contracts/{id}/export` returns the contract as an ODCS document (JSON, or YAML with
`?format=yaml`): the stored document plus `dataq.*` custom properties naming the check behind each
rule, and every check people added to the suites as a `type: custom, engine: dataq` rule.
Importing the export recreates every check.

## Who sees a contract

You see a contract when you can view at least one of its suites; the response counts the linked
suites you cannot see without naming them. Workspace admins also see contracts with no linked
suite. Deleting a contract needs edit on all of its suites, and only unlinks them: no suite, check
or result is deleted.

## Contracts and comparison checks

A [comparison check](datasources-checks.md) reconciles two datasets against each other. A contract
describes one dataset against a written promise. They answer different questions and can be used
together.

def _suites_to_repoint(
    session: Session, odcs_id: str, suite_ids: list[uuid.UUID], *, actor_id: uuid.UUID
) -> list[Suite]:
    """The suites a new version takes over: each `edit`-able and linked to an earlier version
    of the SAME contract (422 otherwise — re-pointing a stranger's suite is not an import)."""
    suites: list[Suite] = []
    for suite_id in dict.fromkeys(suite_ids):
        suite = suite_authz.require_permission(session, suite_id, actor_id, minimum="edit")
        linked = session.get(Contract, suite.contract_id) if suite.contract_id else None
        if linked is None or linked.odcs_id != odcs_id:
            raise ContractSuitesInvalidError(
                "a suite named in suite_ids is not linked to an earlier version of this contract",
                detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id)},
            )
        suites.append(suite)
    return suites

def _visible(session: Session, contract: Contract, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> VisibleContract | None:
    """A contract is visible when the caller can `view` at least one linked suite, or is a
    workspace admin (who also sees a contract with no linked suite)."""
    suites = list(contract.suites)

def list_contracts(session: Session, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> list[VisibleContract]:
    rows = session.scalars(
        select(Contract)
        .options(selectinload(Contract.suites))
        .order_by(Contract.name, Contract.version)
    )
    return [v for c in rows if (v := _visible(session, c, user_id)) is not None]


def get_contract(session: Session, contract_id: uuid.UUID, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> VisibleContract:
    """404 — never 403 — for a contract the caller cannot see (ADR 0027's no-leak rule)."""
    contract = session.get(Contract, contract_id)
    visible = _visible(session, contract, user_id) if contract is not None else None
    if visible is None:
        raise ContractNotFoundError("contract not found", detail={"contract_id": str(contract_id)})
    return visible


def delete_contract(session: Session, contract_id: uuid.UUID, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> None:
    """Unlink the contract's suites (both columns, together) and delete the row; suites, checks
    and results stay. Requires `edit` on every linked suite — unlinking is a suite mutation."""
    visible = get_contract(session, contract_id, user_id)
    for suite in visible.contract.suites:
        suite_authz.require_permission(session, suite.id, user_id, minimum="edit")
    for suite in visible.contract.suites:
        suite.contract_id = None
        suite.contract_object = None
    audit_service.record(
        session,
        action="contract.delete",
        entity_type="contract",
        entity_id=visible.contract.id,
        actor=user_id,
        before={
            "id": str(visible.contract.id),
            "odcs_id": visible.contract.odcs_id,
            "version": visible.contract.version,
            "suites_unlinked": len(visible.contract.suites),
        },
    )
    session.delete(visible.contract)
    session.commit()

def latest_runs_per_suite_stmt(
    suite_scope: Select[tuple[uuid.UUID]] | Sequence[uuid.UUID],
    *,
    as_of: datetime | None = None,
) -> Select[Any]:
    """`SELECT DISTINCT ON (suite_id) * FROM runs …` — each suite's newest run, or
    with ``as_of`` the newest one created at or before that moment.
    """
    stmt = select(Run).where(Run.suite_id.in_(suite_scope))
    if as_of is not None:
        stmt = stmt.where(Run.created_at <= as_of)
    return stmt.order_by(Run.suite_id, Run.created_at.desc(), Run.id.desc()).distinct(Run.suite_id)


def score_as_of(
    session: Session, suite_ids: Sequence[uuid.UUID], as_of: datetime, weights: Weights
) -> float | None:
    """The health score these suites' latest complete runs gave as of ``as_of`` — the
    same latest-run-per-suite rule as the current score, moved back in time. ``None``
    when nothing had evaluated by then.
    """
    if not suite_ids:
        return None
    # A run still in flight at `as_of` had no verdict yet, whatever its status is today.
    run_ids = [
        r.id
        for r in session.scalars(latest_runs_per_suite_stmt(suite_ids, as_of=as_of))
        if r.finished_at is None or r.finished_at <= as_of
    ]
    counts: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    for by_status in status_histograms(session, run_ids, complete_runs_only=True).values():
        for status, n in by_status.items():
            counts[status] += n
    return health_score(counts, weights)

def _latest_run_per_suite(session: Session, suite_ids: list[uuid.UUID]) -> dict[uuid.UUID, Run]:
    """The most-recent run for each suite (DISTINCT ON, newest `created_at`)."""
    if not suite_ids:

    rows = session.scalars(latest_runs_per_suite_stmt(suite_ids))
    return {run.suite_id: run for run in rows}

# ───────────────────────────── compliance ───────────────────────────


#: A clause's state in the rollup — the result its check produced in the suite's latest run, or why
#: there is none. `not_enforced` clauses are the contract's `unmapped` list, reported beside these.
CLAUSE_STATES = ("pass", "warn", "fail", "critical", "unverified", "not_run", "disabled")
_FINAL_RUN_STATUSES = frozenset({"succeeded", "failed", "cancelled"})
_RESULT_STATE = {"pass": "pass", "warn": "warn", "fail": "fail", "critical": "critical"}


@dataclass
class ClauseState:
    suite_id: uuid.UUID
    check_id: uuid.UUID
    check_name: str
    clause: dict[str, Any]
    state: str
    #: The check was edited since its import, so it may no longer say what the clause says.
    drifted: bool


@dataclass
class SuiteCompliance:
    suite_id: uuid.UUID
    last_run_id: uuid.UUID | None
    last_run_status: str | None
    last_run_at: Any
    #: False while the latest run is still queued or running: its results are partial, and the
    #: states below are not a verdict yet.
    results_final: bool


@dataclass
class Compliance:
    clauses: list[ClauseState]
    suites: list[SuiteCompliance]
    counts: dict[str, int]
    not_enforced: int


def compliance(session: Session, visible: VisibleContract) -> Compliance:
    """Per clause, what the check that enforces it found in its suite's latest run — over the
    suites the caller can see only (the restricted ones are counted on the contract, never
    read). One query for the latest runs and one for their results."""
    from backend.app.db.models import Result
    from backend.app.services.rollup import latest_runs_per_suite_stmt

    suite_ids = [s.id for s in visible.suites]
    runs = {
        r.suite_id: r for r in session.scalars(latest_runs_per_suite_stmt(suite_ids))
    } if suite_ids else {}
    run_ids = [r.id for r in runs.values()]
    by_check: dict[uuid.UUID, str] = {}
    if run_ids:
        for result in session.scalars(select(Result).where(Result.run_id.in_(run_ids))):
            by_check[result.check_id] = result.status
    clauses: list[ClauseState] = []
    suites: list[SuiteCompliance] = []
    for suite in visible.suites:
        run = runs.get(suite.id)
        suites.append(
            SuiteCompliance(
                suite_id=suite.id,
                last_run_id=run.id if run else None,
                last_run_status=run.status if run else None,
                last_run_at=(run.finished_at or run.created_at) if run else None,
                results_final=run is not None and run.status in _FINAL_RUN_STATUSES,
            )
        )
        for check in suite.checks:
            if check.origin != CONTRACT_CHECK_ORIGIN or not check.contract_ref:
                continue
            ref = check.contract_ref
            if not check.enabled:
                state = "disabled"
            elif check.id not in by_check:
                state = "not_run"
            else:
                state = _RESULT_STATE.get(by_check[check.id], "unverified")
            stored = ref.get("fingerprint")
            clauses.append(
                ClauseState(
                    suite_id=suite.id,
                    check_id=check.id,
                    check_name=check.name,
                    clause={k: ref.get(k) for k in ("object", "property", "rule_id", "field")},
                    state=state,
                    drifted=stored is not None and stored != _current_fingerprint(check),
                )
            )
    counts = {state: 0 for state in CLAUSE_STATES}
    for clause in clauses:
        counts[clause.state] += 1
    return Compliance(
        clauses=clauses,
        suites=suites,
        counts=counts,
        not_enforced=len(visible.contract.unmapped or []),
    )

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" 2>&1 | grep -iv "passed\|skipped"; git push -q 2>&1 | grep -v "entire\|^remote"; reply() { gh api -X POST repos/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pulls/2552/comments/$1/replies -f body="$2" --jq .id >/dev/null; }
F=$(git log --format=%h -2 | tail -1); G=$(git log --format=%h -1)
reply 4370721593 "Fixed in $F: linking into a contract now needs \`edit\` on every suite already linked (the same gate replace and delete use, via \`_require_edit_on_all\`), so a view-only collaborator cannot attach a suite and lock the owner out. Test covers it; mutation-checked."
reply 4370721646 "Fixed in $F: a link is refused when another linked suite already stands for that object."
reply 4370721724 "Fixed in $F: a link is refused when the contract's other suites run on a different connection."
reply 4370721761 "Fixed in $F: each contract-derived check's clause records the contract's \`odcs_id\`; the evidence layer returns null and the rollup skips the clause when the suite's current contract is a different one. Test relinks a suite to another contract and asserts both; mutation-checked."
reply 4370721834 "Fixed in $F: \`results_final\` is true only for a \`succeeded\` run (\`rollup.AGGREGATABLE_RUN_STATUSES\`); \`not_run\` is documented to cover a run that stopped early. Test with a cancelled run."
reply 4370721872 "Fixed in $F: one query for the suites' contract checks and one for \`(check_id, status)\` of the latest runs' results; full rows are no longer loaded."
reply 4370721932 "Fixed in $F: missing parts are left out (no doubled space, no \`None\`); test for both shapes."
reply 4370721978 "Fixed in $F: the state reuses \`RESULT_SEVERITY_TIERS\` from models."
reply 4370722058 "Fixed in $F: the detail response is built once from \`ContractRead.fields_of\`."
reply 4370722131 "Fixed in $F: the models import is at module top."
reply 4370723493 "Fixed in $G: \`suite_service.update_suite\` takes an \`apply_contract_link\` callable that the route supplies, so suite_service no longer imports contract_service at all; the link still happens inside the same transaction and \`suite.update\` audit event."
gh api graphql -f query='{repository(owner:"TheurgicDuke771",name:"DataQ"){pullRequest(number:2552){reviewThreads(first:40){nodes{id isResolved}}}}}' --jq '.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[] | select(.isResolved==false) | .id' | while read t; do gh api graphql -f query="mutation{resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:\"$t\"}){thread{isResolved}}}" --jq '.data.resolveReviewThread.thread.isResolved'; done | sort | uniq -c
input.description: Commit and push the cycle fix; reply to and resolve all eleven threads on PR 2552
